A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CORE research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Textual and visual inspection supports a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments, conceptual diagnostics, robustness tests, ablations, and the PPO-based experiment in Appendix C.1.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: CORE-Base, conditional trajectory replacement, concept-guided KL regularization, and the appendix PPO instantiation are unchanged. The redrawn Figure 2 depicts the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same textbook corpus, synthetic quizzes, 140-exercise evaluation set, out-of-domain benchmarks, and perturbation scenarios. Appendix C.1 also retains the same benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same participants, including Vanilla, SFT, Random-Reward GRPO, Top 4 of 6 GRPO, and CORE-Base + Verifier. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, evaluation subsets, and testing procedures are unchanged. Both retain SC@21 at temperature 0.7, the same option-permutation protocol, and the same distractor evaluation design.

E4.justification: The concept-selection diagnostic, irrelevant-concept robustness tests, GRPO controls, self-supervised experiment, and verifier comparison are retained. Appendix C preserves both the PPO analysis and orthogonal-matrix case study.

E5.justification: Both versions specify a single random seed for the fixed distractor sets in Section 5.2. Neither adds repeated-training-run statistics, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched results in Tables 1–9 and Figure 3 are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains Textbook accuracies of 46.4 for Vanilla, 52.1 for CORE-CR, and 55.7 for CORE-KL.

T1.justification: The KL objective in Equation (1), the retention metric definition in Section 5.2, and the PPO return and advantage formulations in Equations (2)–(3) are unchanged. No formal result or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about bridging the definition–application gap, improving conceptual reasoning and robustness, and compatibility with policy-gradient algorithms.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning concept selection, robustness, model generality, and independence from superior teacher models are unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: The data-curation instructions, hardware, hyperparameters, decoding procedure, training prompt, and resource references are unchanged. Appendices A–B and the reproducibility statement provide the same information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including Section 2 and the comparison with BREAD in Section 3.4. The added conference header does not revise the scientific positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds the ICLR 2026 publication header and changes title styling. Substantive prose, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged; passage movements follow page reflow.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with rounded panels, revised icons and arrows, and a recolored KL illustration with explicit axis labels. Headers and page reflow alter placement, while other figures and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The sharper artwork, separated panels, and clearer branch routing in Figure 2 modestly improve communication of the existing framework. The scientific evidence, analysis, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall benefit is limited to presentation.
